contentHtml:
Christmas charcuterie board transforms your table into a wintery feast, layered with rosemary sprigs, sparkling pomegranate arils, and ruby cranberries beside tender turkey and roast beef. Creamy brie and tangy goat cheese shine next to sweet fig spread, crunchy multiseed crackers, and a drizzle of honey over rosemary kissed cheese for that festive glow. Add a non alcoholic sparkling cider reduction for a bright, faux bubbly finish, then scatter toasted almonds and pistachios for irresistible crunch. Easy to assemble and gorgeous to serve, this christmas charcuterie board sets the tone for cozy fireside snacking, laughter, and holiday warmth in every bite.

Why You’ll Love This christmas charcuterie board

  • Perfect for sharing with family and friends during the festive season.
  • Customizable with your favorite cheeses, fruits, and nuts.
  • Visually stunning centerpiece that adds holiday cheer to any gathering.
  • Easy to prepare, allowing you to enjoy more time with loved ones.

christmas charcuterie board

Discover delightful Christmas charcuterie board ideas and easy holiday recipes to impress your guests this festive season! 🎄🧀🥖
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 20 minutes mins
resting 2 hours hrs
Total Time 2 hours hrs 20 minutes mins
Servings: 8 servings
Course: Appetizer, Snacks
Cuisine: American
Calories: 350
Ingredients Equipment Method Notes

Ingredients
  

Cured Meats
  • 200 g assorted cured meats prosciutto, salami, and chorizo
Cheeses
  • 150 g variety of cheeses brie, cheddar, and gouda
Fruits
  • 1 cup fresh fruits grapes, apple slices, and pomegranate seeds
  • 100 g dried fruits figs and apricots
Nuts
  • 75 g nuts almonds and walnuts
Crackers and Breadsticks
  • 1 box crackers and breadsticks assorted
Olives and Pickles
  • 100 g olives and pickles mixed
Honey or Fruit Preserves
  • 100 g honey or fruit preserves for drizzling
Fresh Herbs
  • 1 handful fresh herbs rosemary and thyme
Festive Decorations
  • 50 g festive decorations cranberries and a few rosemary sprigs

Equipment

  • 1 large wooden or slate board This will be the canvas for your festive creation.

Method
 

Step 1: Select a Board
  1. Choose a large wooden or slate board as your base. This will be the canvas for your festive creation.
Step 2: Arrange Cheeses
  1. Place your cheeses first. Space them evenly around the board for a balanced look.
Step 3: Add Cured Meats
  1. Fold or roll your cured meats. Position them next to the cheeses for a delightful pairing.
Step 4: Include Small Bowls
  1. Add small bowls filled with olives, pickles, honey, or preserves. These will add flavor and variety.
Step 5: Fill with Fruits
  1. Fill any gaps with fresh and dried fruits. Spread the colors evenly for a vibrant display.
Step 6: Scatter Nuts
  1. Scatter nuts around the board. This adds texture and a delightful crunch.
Step 7: Add Crackers and Breadsticks
  1. Place crackers and breadsticks in clusters. This makes it easy for guests to grab and enjoy.
Step 8: Garnish
  1. Garnish your board with fresh herbs and festive decorations like cranberries. This adds a cheerful touch.
Step 9: Serve
  1. Serve immediately or cover lightly with plastic wrap. You can refrigerate it for up to 2 hours before serving.

Recipe Snapshot

Pro Tips for Making christmas charcuterie board

  • Incorporate a variety of cheeses like cheddar, gouda, and brie for diverse flavors.
  • Add seasonal fruits like pomegranate seeds and clementines for a festive touch.
  • Include nuts and dried fruits for texture and sweetness.
  • Use colorful veggies like bell peppers and cherry tomatoes for a vibrant look.
  • Arrange items in groups for an inviting and organized presentation.

How to Serve this christmas charcuterie board

  • Arrange a variety of cheeses like cheddar, gouda, and brie for a delightful mix.
  • Include seasonal fruits such as pomegranate seeds, figs, and apple slices for a pop of color.
  • Add crunchy nuts like almonds and walnuts for texture and flavor.
  • Incorporate festive crackers and breadsticks for dipping and spreading.
  • Offer a selection of spreads like hummus, fig jam, and honey for extra sweetness.
  • Garnish with fresh herbs like rosemary and thyme for a holiday touch.
  • Serve with sparkling water or non-alcoholic cider for a refreshing drink option.
  • Use a large wooden board or platter to create an inviting centerpiece.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing and enjoying your Christmas charcuterie board leftovers is easy:

Storing Leftovers

  • Place leftovers in an airtight container.
  • Refrigerate within two hours of serving.
  • Consume within 3-4 days for best quality.

Freezing

  • Wrap individual items tightly in plastic wrap.
  • Place wrapped items in a freezer-safe bag or container.
  • Label with the date and contents.
  • Use within 1-2 months for optimal flavor.

Reheating

  • Thaw in the refrigerator overnight before reheating.
  • Use a microwave or oven at low heat.
  • Cover with a damp paper towel in the microwave.
  • Avoid overheating to maintain texture.

FAQs

Here’s a helpful FAQ about this recipe:

1. What is the 3-3-3 rule for charcuterie boards?

The 3-3-3 rule for charcuterie boards suggests including three types of cheese, three types of meat, and three types of accompaniments. This balanced approach ensures a variety of flavors and textures, making your Christmas charcuterie board both visually appealing and delicious. You can substitute meats with plant-based options like hummus, roasted vegetables, or marinated tofu to keep it festive and inclusive for all dietary preferences.

2. What do you put on a Christmas charcuterie board?

A Christmas charcuterie board can be filled with a delightful mix of seasonal items. Consider including a variety of cheeses such as brie, cheddar, and goat cheese, along with an assortment of crackers and breadsticks. Add fresh fruits like grapes, figs, or pomegranate seeds for a pop of color, and include nuts, olives, and pickles for added crunch. For a festive touch, incorporate holiday-themed items like cranberry sauce or spiced nuts, and don’t forget some sweet treats like chocolate or gingerbread cookies to round out the experience!

3. What is replacing charcuterie boards?

While charcuterie boards remain popular, some are opting for ‘grazing tables’ or ‘snack boards’ that offer a wider variety of foods beyond meats and cheeses. These can include a mix of fruits, vegetables, dips, and even desserts, allowing for more creativity and personalization. The focus is on creating a communal experience where guests can enjoy a diverse selection of flavors, making it perfect for holiday gatherings like Christmas parties!

4. How to put together a Christmas charcuterie board?

To assemble a Christmas charcuterie board, start by selecting a large wooden board or platter as your base. Begin by arranging your cheeses, cutting them into various shapes for visual interest. Next, add your plant-based meats or alternatives, followed by crackers and bread. Fill in the gaps with fresh fruits, nuts, and any festive decorations like sprigs of rosemary or edible flowers. Finally, include small bowls of dips or spreads, and don’t forget to add some sweet treats for a delightful finish. The key is to create a colorful and inviting display that encourages sharing and enjoyment!

Final Thoughts

As you gather around your festive Christmas charcuterie board, remember that the joy is in the sharing! With vibrant colors and delightful flavors, this simple yet rewarding creation will spark laughter and warm memories. So, grab your favorite cheeses, fruits, and nuts, and let the holiday spirit shine through every bite. Enjoy the magic of the season!
